why: the README describes live pull requests, and a description that is not checked against them drifts. An external reviewer found this table contradicting its own repository: it named a workflow state that had changed, and called #3 a case where Gate has nothing to say when Gate says the same thing about it as about #1.

ruleset.name: Require all tests passed
ruleset.why: without it the demonstration shows a check that blocks nothing, which is the opposite of the point

app.why: every scenario must be analysed by the PRODUCTION App. Two of these were analysed by arcifact-gate-dev, so the demonstration showed output no visitor could reproduce.

pulls.why_it_matters: the required check passes and the change is a reduction. This is the gap.

pulls.change: narrows the aggregate to pull_request only
the same drop as #1, with its own CI failing for an unrelated reason
pulls.why_it_matters: Gate reports the same reduction as #1. The platform blocks this one anyway, so Gate adds nothing you would not already know. Included because a demonstration that only shows the tool winning is one nobody should trust.

what_this_file_is_for: verify.py checks every claim here against the live repository. If the README and the repository disagree, that is a failure rather than a documentation chore.
